title: A 300MB SRAM, 20Tb/s Bandwidth Scalable Heterogenous 2.5D System Inferencing Simultaneous Streams Across 20 Chiplets with Workload-Dependent Configurations
problem: Large AI systems face memory-bandwidth and memory-capacity bottlenecks. Chiplet-based architectures enable modularity and technology heterogeneity but require scalable on-chip memory and high-bandwidth interconnects. Traditional monolithic designs cannot support diverse workload-dependent resource allocation at assembly time.
motivation: AI inference workloads have heterogeneous compute/memory/bandwidth demands. Disaggregated 2.5D systems should enable post-fabrication workload customization, optimal resource allocation, and processing of voluminous datasets across multiple streams.
method: The system stacks 20 small chips (chiplets) in layers connected by extremely fast data highways (20Tb/s, meaning 20 trillion bits per second). All chips share 300MB of high-speed memory (SRAM) split across the stack. Before assembly finishes, engineers customize each chip's computing power, memory allotment, and bandwidth based on the AI inference tasks the system will handle. The chips can come from different manufacturers and technology generations, so each can be optimized for its specific job in the overall system.
key_novelty: This reconfigurable 2.5D chiplet system allocates its memory, computing power, and bandwidth differently depending on each AI inference workload.
contributions: 300MB distributed SRAM supporting multiple simultaneous inference streams
Workload-dependent assembly-time configuration enabling optimal resource allocation
Heterogeneous technology integration from multiple foundries per chiplet
primary_theme: Scalable chiplet-based system for workload-customized AI inference
